newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AGL says interest in NSW power distribution.
newsitem.headline: AGL says interest in NSW power distribution.

text.p: The Australian Gas Light Co said on Thursday it was more interested in distribution than power generation if the New South Wales state government privatised its power industry.
"We are interested in it all, but we are more interested in the distribution and the transmission than we are interested in the power generation," said managing director Len Bleasel.
"As we didn't bid in Victoria on power generation it can be assumed we probably won't bid in New South Wales," he told reporters after an address to the Australian Institute of Company Directors.
The New South Wales state government has set up a committee of inquiry to advise on the mooted sell-off of its electricty industry, which it says could raise up to A$22 billion.
A wide range of international and domestic parties would be expected to bid, following similar interest in Victoria's power sell-off during the past three years.
Bleasel said power generators would be very expensive and such a commitment could rule out other opportunities for AGL.
The gas and electricty distributor is also interested in the break-up and privatisation of Victoria's GasCor and in pipelines in Western Australia and from Papua New Guinea to Australia.
"There are more opportunities than we have dollars," Bleasel said.
